hadith:
Asking Permission - Narrated `Aisha:

A group of Jews came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "As-samu 'Alaika " (Death be on you), and I understood it and said to them, "Alaikum AsSamu wa-l-la'na (Death and curse be on you)." Allah's Apostle said, "Be calm! O `Aisha, for Allah loves that one should be kind and lenient in all matters." I said. "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Haven't you heard what they have said?" Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "I have (already) said (to them), 'Alaikum (upon you).' "
message: When facing difficulties, remember that only Allah can truly harm or benefit you, so place your trust entirely in Him. Following the Prophet's example of kindness and gentleness—even toward those who oppose you—reflects the majesty of Al Maajid, the Glorious, in your character. By combining reliance on Allah with compassionate conduct, you honor His greatness and draw closer to Him.
name:
Al Maajid - الْمَاجِدُ - The Glorious

The name Al Maajid emphasizes the glory and majesty of Allah. It highlights His honor and the reverence He commands in the hearts of believers. The origin of this name comes from the Arabic root related to honor and magnificence, reflecting the Islamic belief in Allah's supremacy and grandeur in all aspects of existence.
verse:
Al-Jinn - The Jinn - 72:20-22

Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I call only upon my Lord, associating none with Him ˹in worship˺.”

Say, “It is not in my power to harm or benefit you.”

Say, “No one can protect me from Allah ˹if I were to disobey Him˺, nor can I find any refuge other than Him.
